summary: Ground lookout on Goat Hill, south of the Mount Lassic summit in Humboldt County; FFLOS lists it gone; a 2023 hike found only a scaffold.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; a 2023 blog visit found only a scaffold at the site.

access.note: A 2023 blog walked up national forest roads to the site and describes no closure there; a second road or trail is no longer legal for motor vehicles.

visit.trail_note: A 2023 blog hike went up South Goat Hill Road, a high-clearance road the writer found legal to drive.

events.note: Lassics Fire; the 2023 blog describes standing dead and burned trunks along South Goat Hill Road and does not say the lookout site burned.

evidence.supports: The lookout stood on Goat Hill, south of the summit.
evidence.quote: it was placed on Goat Hill to the south

evidence.supports: The summit's concrete survey pillar is a trig station.

evidence.supports: The writer first wondered whether the summit marker was part of an old lookout.
evidence.quote: I actually wondered if it was some piece of an old fire lookout when I first saw it.

evidence.supports: The summit's official name, Signal Peak, traces back to a heliograph station that stood on it around 1900.
evidence.quote: The official name, Signal Peak, derives from the heliograph station that was located on this peak around 1900.

evidence.supports: Signal Peak is also called Mount Lassic.
evidence.quote: Signal Peak , or Mount Lassic , is a summit in the Coast Range of Humboldt County

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLOS record for Lassic, Mount sits south of the summit coordinates Wikipedia gives for Signal Peak. The 2023 blog places the lookout on Goat Hill, south of the summit, so the record appears to mark Goat Hill rather than the summit. Not checked against a Goat Hill coordinate.

notes_for_editor: No build date, builder, staffing history or removal date appears in any source I could read, so the story has no built or staffing section and no removal date. Only two blog posts describe the site itself, and both are 2023 visits. The record's name and coordinates (40.2964, -123.5515) fit a Goat Hill site, but no Goat Hill coordinate was checked. The 2023 blog refers to 'the lookouts' in the plural when describing a water source, so the number of lookout structures is unverified. A Moments in Dirt and Ink Facebook post about a removed lookout on Goat Hill returned only its title in the crawl, so it is not cited. Research budget exceeded: four searches and about 16 page reads, against a budget of two and six per tower.
